newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee flat, banks watch call rates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee flat, banks watch call rates.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was barely moved in dull trade, as call money continued to set the pace for movements in the dollar-rupee exchange rate, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.57 to the dollar, after opening at its previous closing level of 56.55, they said.
"With hardly any genuine demand for dollars, interest rates continued to impact on the exchange rate," said a Citibank dealer.
Dollar demand was sluggish for most of the month due to high money rates, which rose as high as 30 percent, he said.
Dealers said money was high and volatile due to seasonal demand for rupees, which sent banks in search of short-term funding.
Call money closed at 22 percent after opening at 27 today, with a big state bank lending throughout the day, dealers said.
"But just because call rates dipped on one day, I do not think the exchange rate is going to pick up," said the Citibank dealer.
